source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Apply only within formal research studies, rather than to routine, ongoing hospital care delivery, similar to what the new administrator is currently assuming","B":"Have little established connection to the overall quality of care a hospital provides its patients, contrary to why these measures are actually tracked","C":"Fully replace the need for individualized clinical judgment at the bedside for these conditions, which is not the actual purpose of these particular measures","D":"Assess adherence to evidence-based care processes shown to improve patient outcomes, rather than serving a purely research purpose as the new administrator assumed"}}
source_row.rationale: Core measures are standardized, evidence-based care process indicators used to assess adherence to practices shown to improve patient outcomes for specific conditions, supporting quality improvement.
source_row.stem: A hospital tracks compliance with standardized "core measures" for conditions like heart failure and pneumonia, and a new administrator assumes these measures exist mainly for research purposes rather than for the hospital's actual day-to-day patient care.
